title: fix(plugin-chatbot): merge an authored className into the floating chat panel
body:
Fixes #8078

## What changed

`FloatingChatbot` ended its `ChatbotEnhanced` element with a bare
`className="h-full border-0 rounded-none"` literal written **after** the
`chatbotProps` spread. A later JSX prop always beats an earlier spread, so the
`className` a `chatbot-floating` node authored — correctly forwarded the whole
way, since the registration destructures `className` as its own named prop —
was silently replaced, never appended. It type-checked, it parsed, and it did
nothing to the rendered panel: the styling escape hatch AGENTS.md #3 requires
every widget to expose ("Always expose `className` in schema props so users can
override via JSON"), exposed and inert. Every sibling in this package already
merges through `cn()` — `ChatbotEnhanced` calls it throughout, which is the
in-package control that makes this drift rather than design.

The line is now `className={cn("h-full border-0 rounded-none", chatbotProps.className)}`.

## The measurement the route turned on

The dispatch was explicit that the argument order is decided by measurement, not
by reasoning about `cn`. Measured — and measured through the render, not by
reading the helper:

- `@object-ui/components` exports `cn` as `twMerge(clsx(inputs))`, with
  `tailwind-merge` 3.6.0 resolved in this workspace. `plugin-chatbot` imports
  `cn` from that package, which is the same `cn` `ChatbotEnhanced` uses.
- The live proof is the CONTROL case of the new pin. A `chatbot-floating` node
  authoring no `className` renders exactly
  `flex min-h-0 flex-col overflow-hidden bg-background h-full border-0 rounded-none`.
  Note what is absent: `ChatbotEnhanced` contributes `rounded-lg border` to that
  same element, and the merge with `border-0 rounded-none` REMOVED both. That is
  last-conflicting-utility-wins, observed on the rendered element rather than
  inferred from the helper's source.

⇒ Panel classes FIRST, the author's declaration LAST. That is the opposite of
the order the card suggested, and the inversion is the point: under
tailwind-merge, putting the author first would have kept overriding the author —
by merge ordering instead of by replacement — which is the trap triage named.

## The three outcomes the dispatch set

1. **An author who declares a different border or corner radius gets it.**
   `rounded-xl` and `border-2` reach the rendered panel and the panel's
   `rounded-none` / `border-0` are gone. Pinned.
2. **The panel still fits its container when the author declares nothing about
   size.** `h-full` survives the merge, and an unstyled node's class list is
   byte-identical to the pre-fix face. Both pinned. An author who DOES declare a
   size (`h-64`) replaces `h-full` — that is exactly the boundary the dispatch
   drew ("when the author declares nothing about size"), pinned as its own case.
3. **What the panel keeps by force carries a comment at the line** naming why it
   is load-bearing.

Outcomes 1 and 2 are satisfiable together under this repo's `cn`; no ruling
about what a floating panel may own was needed.

## The `maxHeight` ruling — it is NOT a second instance, and here is why

Triage was right that `maxHeight="100%"` two lines up has the identical SHAPE.
It is not, however, the same defect, and the difference is decisive: there is no
authored value for it to drop.

- `ChatbotFloatingSchema` does not declare `maxHeight` at all. Its own docblock
  states the key is "NOT declared, on purpose", and gives this exact mechanism as
  the reason — the panel pins its inner chat to `100%` of the panel height, after
  any forwarded value.
- The `chatbot-floating` registration forwards no `maxHeight` prop either, while
  its two siblings (`chatbot`, `chatbot-enhanced`) both do. The published
  retirement note on the `height` tombstone records `maxHeight` as read 1 / 1 / 0
  across the three registrations — zero for this one.
- `className` is the opposite case: it IS declared on this face, inherited from
  `BaseSchema`, and the same docblock says so.

So the twin is **deliberately owned by the panel**, and it is load-bearing:
`ChatbotEnhanced` defaults `maxHeight` to `'500px'`, which would cap the
conversation well inside a panel that can be 800px tall — or the whole viewport
in fullscreen. The ruling is recorded in a comment at the line and pinned by the
control case, which asserts the rendered panel still carries `max-height: 100%`.

⚠️ One thing this does leave standing, deliberately: `FloatingChatbotProps`
inherits `maxHeight` from `ChatbotEnhancedProps`, so a DIRECT React consumer of
the exported component still has that value forced away. See Acceptance notes.

## Tests

The card recorded that it had measured the defect statically and "not yet
confirmed through a live render", and triage asked the fixing PR to close that
rather than inherit it. It is closed here.

New pin `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/__tests__/FloatingChatbot.classNameMerge-8078.test.tsx`
mounts a `chatbot-floating` node through the real SDUI host (`SchemaRenderer`,
the registry, the real portal) and asserts on the rendered panel's own class
list — the element found by the `data-obj-id` the host derives from the node id.

Reverse verification, from the committed fix, with the mutation proven on disk
(the `cn(...)` spelling went 1 occurrence to 0 and the bare literal 0 to 1, and
the mutated blob hash differed from the HEAD blob) and the restore proven
(restored blob hash equal to the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty):

| leg | result |
|---|---|
| pre-fix tree, pin added | `Tests 2 failed, 1 passed (3)` — the authored `bg-amber-50` and `h-64` never reached the panel |
| fix applied | `Tests 3 passed (3)` |
| fix committed, then mutated back to the literal | `Tests 2 failed, 1 passed (3)` |
| restored from HEAD | `Tests 3 passed (3)` |

The control passes on BOTH sides, which is what makes it a control: the unstyled
face does not move.

## Acceptance notes

- **Noted, not filed:** `FloatingChatbotProps` inherits `maxHeight` from
  `ChatbotEnhancedProps`, so the value is declared on the exported React props
  type and is still forced away for a direct React consumer. Not filed as a
  finding: a React prop is not authored metadata, and no declared contract is
  contradicted — the authoring face documents the panel pinning its inner chat as
  deliberate. There is also no consumer today: outside this plugin's own
  registration, this repo has zero call sites of the exported component. Handler
  if it ever matters: none today. Honouring it would need the panel-ownership
  ruling reopened, which is a contract decision, not a merge.
- Scope held to this one file. objectui#7708 covers the registration-level spread
  one file over and is untouched here; the objectui#4425 / objectui#4431
  `toDomProps` family is the opposite axis (extra attributes reaching the DOM)
  and is untouched too. `ChatbotEnhanced.tsx` is the control and was not edited.

## Clause-2 re-measurement

`no`, re-measured rather than inherited: the diff adds no exported symbol, no key
on any published payload, no Zod arm, and relaxes no acceptance set —
`ChatbotFloatingSchema` and `FloatingChatbotProps` are unchanged, and `className`
was already declared on this authoring face through `BaseSchema` and already
parsed. ⚠️ Boundary flag for the reviewing seat: what DOES move is an
already-declared key going from inert to honoured, which is the "fills an
already-declared field" conformance shape the seat's own reference marks as
judgement rather than mechanism. Flagged rather than decided here.
